summary: 18.1 'Which projects the hook treats as Greenfield-Senior' says removing or moving .eccode/events.jsonl 'is a write the hook refuses to the file tools (RECORD_FILES), and for a group role it would need the shell that GF-RUN-1 denies', and the 18.3 table says a forged append 'needs a writer other than the hook-covered tools' and is stopped by 'the hook (RECORD_FILES)'. But 18.3 and 18.4 give every group role the runner, which runs project code (for example its own tests under pytest) that 'can write' any file, with the run failed afterwards and 'the change itself is not undone (L-GF-29)'. Section 18 does not say what holds when such a run deletes or appends to events.jsonl (by 18.1 a missing log switches off GF-OWN-2 and GF-RUN-1 for the hook), so the stated protection of the record, and of Greenfield-Senior detection, is contradicted by the runner route the same section describes.

18.3 'The hook's identity check, stated precisely': the main session 'is denied any other ECCode role unless ECCODE_SEQUENTIAL_ROLES=1 is set, a mode that must be disclosed to the person', and the next sentence concludes unconditionally 'So the orchestrator cannot record a closing review under a reviewer role through a command the hook can read'. Under that mode it can. Section 18 does not say where the variable is read (the hook's process, the command), whether the mode is recorded or reported anywhere (the F0 preflight list does not name it), who enforces 'must be disclosed', or what then remains of GF-CLOSE-1 independence (18.5 'Closure independence rests on the same controls' omits it).

18.4 states the runner accepts 'a command the plan already pins ... or a command in a pinned form of one of eight tools', then 'A command is words separated by single spaces ... anything else ... is shell syntax and is refused'. It does not say whether that grammar applies to plan-pinned commands (task checks often contain '&&' or a 'cd'), nor how a plan-pinned command is executed; 18.7 'Survivors' then reveals that 'a plan-pinned command that starts with an environment assignment runs through the shell' (runner.js:191). A reader cannot tell which plan-pinned commands are refused, which run through a shell for a role that 'has no shell', and which run directly.

18.5 GF-CLOSE-3 requires batteries that are 'pinned mutation runs' and judges 'the last valid battery recorded for the scope', but section 18 never defines what is pinned or what makes a battery valid: the command takes '--test <command> --base <commit> [--max <n>]' and section 18 does not say whether the test command, the base commit or the mutant count are checked (a '--test false' or a base equal to HEAD would trivially leave no survivor). Only L-GF-26 says these are 'the orchestrator's choice', and section 18 cites L-GF-26 solely for counter resets (18.6).

18.5: 'every valid review of a step on the closing tree counts', and 'A valid review, stated once' lists only form conditions; GF-CLOSE-1 requires 'each recorded by a configured reviewer role that authored nothing in the record ... and is not the closer'; 18.7 round 3 says 'a closing review recorded by the closer does not count' (D3-1). Section 18 does not state what happens to a form-valid review by a role that fails the independence condition: whether it is refused when recorded, ignored at close, or blocks the close; whether its findings must still be resolved under GF-CLOSE-2 ('every finding of every review of the scope'); and whether its readiness no-go 'stands'.

18.3 table, shell row: 'the hook on command text (limits rows 91, 117: text-level, obfuscation can pass)'. The register is not named, and rows 91 and 117 of docs/limits.md describe false refusals by the text guard (a read-only program refused; a whole-line identity rule holding a command), not that obfuscation can pass; the cited rows do not support the claim made with them.

18.7 'Survivors' describes the first, second, third, fourth, fifth and then 'The seventh (tree 539add4, after round 6's fixes ...)' battery; no sixth battery is described, so a reader cannot tell whether one exists, on which tree it ran, or what its survivors were.

18.6 'Per round': 'Round 5 has its own cap, 100 M (the owner's decision)' does not say what a cap means or what follows if it is exceeded, and the as-built accounting gives figures only to the end of round 4, while 18.4 and 18.7 describe round 5's and round 6's fixes; no figure, and no statement that rounds 5 and 6 are unmeasurable or pending, is given for them.

18.6: 'G0 plus S1 consumed 129.5 M ... S1's registered range was 4 to 8 M. The estimate was off by a factor of 16 to 32 in this unit'. The factor divides a G0-plus-S1 figure by S1's range without saying whether that range covered G0; the paragraph itself says no S1-only snapshot exists, so the stated factor has no like-for-like basis.

18.1 Clarifications: 'the contract files are the five sealed files plus contracts/events.json'. The five files are never named in section 18 (nor is a section cited for them), so the exact set GF-FRZ-1 protects cannot be reconstructed from section 18.

18.1 Clarifications: 'The G1 artifacts live under .eccode/artifacts/ (written by the document authors, delivery-lead included, through the hook's artifact area)'. 'Document authors' and 'the hook's artifact area' are not defined in section 18, and it does not say whether delivery-lead is a group role; if it is, GF-OWN-3 calls every .eccode/ path but drafts 'owned by no group' and GF-OWN-2 refuses a group role's write to such a path, so whether an artifact write by a group role after the seal is allowed cannot be told.

18.5: the event list 'Events: gf.review.recorded, gf.finding.resolved, gf.battery.recorded, gf.slice.closed' omits gf.dispatch.recorded, which GF-CLOSE-5 requires; and GF-CLOSE-5 lists the dispatch's content as '(role, step, tree, inputs with their hashes)' while requiring that a review be 'of that role, that step, that scope and that tree', so whether a dispatch records a scope is not stated.

18.4: 'Writing forms are for group roles only', but only the 'ruff, writing' row is labelled as writing; alembic 'revision' (writes under migrations/), alembic 'upgrade'/'downgrade' (write 'the database') and uvicorn ('what the check writes') are not classified, so which forms a role in no group may run is not stated.
